rectorate.title: Leadership grounded in scholarship
rectorate.subtitle: Meet the Rector and read the welcome that sets the tone for our academic community.

profile.title: Rector’s profile
profile.description: Prof. Dr. hab. Mirosław Kędrzyński-Woźniak is an internationally respected academic, higher education leader, and advocate for peace-focused learning. With a career spanning more than two decades across multiple continents, he brings to Kielce International University a blend of academic rigor, global perspective, and a commitment to socially responsible leadership.
profile.qualifications: He holds a Ph.D. in Political Science and International Relations, with specializations in peace and conflict studies, global diplomacy, and intercultural communication. He has served in academic and administrative roles across Europe, Central Asia, and the Middle East, consistently advancing dialogue, critical thinking, and ethical leadership in higher education.

welcomeMessage.title: Welcome from the Rector
welcomeMessage.paragraph1: Welcome to Kielce International University. It is my honor to greet you at the start of a new academic chapter. We are committed to a supportive, innovative, and inclusive environment where every member of our community can grow.
welcomeMessage.paragraph2: Education here is more than knowledge transfer — it is the practice of critical thinking, creativity, and responsibility to society. I encourage you to use every opportunity, engage with the community, and pursue excellence in your work.
welcomeMessage.paragraph3: Together we will build a brighter future through learning, research, and collaboration. I am confident your time at KIU will be both rigorous and inspiring.
welcomeMessage.closing: I wish you success and fulfillment in your studies and beyond.

faq.title: Fees, answered plainly
faq.subtitle: Quick answers on tuition, payment timing, refunds, and scholarships.

q1.question: What does tuition cover?
q1.answer: Tuition covers your academic courses, core campus facilities (library, labs, computing), student support, and standard student activities. Program-specific materials or optional extras may carry separate fees.

q2.question: Can I pay in installments?
q2.answer: Yes. Choose semester payments, ten monthly installments, or a custom schedule. Interest-free installment options are available — contact finance to set one up.

q3.question: Are there fees beyond tuition?
q3.answer: You may see an application fee, registration fee, student services fee, or pathway-specific costs such as materials or field trips. These are listed in your offer letter and student handbook.

q4.question: Which payment methods are accepted?
q4.answer: Bank transfer, card payments, and approved online platforms. International students may also pay by wire transfer. Full instructions arrive with your enrollment pack.

q5.question: Can I get a refund if I withdraw?
q5.answer: Refund rules depend on your program and when you withdraw. Partial refunds are often available early in the semester and decrease later. Your enrollment agreement has the full policy.

q6.question: Are scholarships renewable?
q6.answer: Most awards renew yearly if you keep the required academic standing (often GPA 3.0+), stay enrolled full-time, and remain in good standing. Check your award letter for exact terms.

q7.question: Can I apply for more than one scholarship?
q7.answer: Yes. Combined aid cannot exceed the total cost of attendance; we help you assemble the strongest eligible package.

q8.question: When are fees due?
q8.answer: Full payment is due before each semester starts. Semester plans bill at term start. Monthly plans usually run for ten months from September. Exact dates are in your enrollment package.

q9.question: Is there an early-payment discount?
q9.answer: Yes — 10% for paying in full upfront, and 5% for semester payments. Discounts apply to tuition only.

q10.question: What if I cannot pay on time?
q10.answer: Contact the finance office as soon as possible. We can discuss plan changes, emergency support, and counseling. Late fees may apply if no arrangement is made in advance.
